memory_update.text: AMKR should be retained as the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for advanced packaging and test capacity, but later layers must separate AI/HPC-specific utilization from broad OSAT cycle recovery.

FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM test candidate because official 2026 disclosures connect record DRAM revenue to increased HBM demand, and product materials tie probe-card architecture to HBM stack and interposer test.

ONTO maps to the inspection/metrology chokepoint inside HBM and advanced packaging; the strongest verification path is backlog and volume purchase agreement conversion for Dragonfly inspection and 3D bump metrology.
COHU is a lower-confidence but useful second-order test-handler/contactors candidate; official materials mention GPU, HBM, and high-end CPU thermal handling, but revenue materiality remains unproven.

Layer 1C should separately search non-US primary listings and ADR/OTC availability for Powertech Technology, ASE Technology, JCET, Hana Micron, Camtek, BESI, Disco, Advantest, and substrate/material suppliers because some of the most direct HBM backend capacity may not be US-listed common equity.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM backend, OSAT, and memory package/test capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that HBM and AI accelerator demand can crowd out conventional memory backend and advanced package/test capacity into qualified OSATs and adjacent test/metrology vendors. The pass intentionally limits mega-cap context and emphasizes second-order beneficiaries: outsourced packaging/test capacity, HBM probe-card/test subsystems, advanced packaging inspection/metrology, and thermal test handlers/contactors. No candidate is a trading recommendation; each is a research candidate requiring revenue-segment and customer-validation follow-up.
